comments.text:
If you enjoyed seeing how life works in the Falklands, watch another remote-life documentary here 👇
👉Living in Palau | How Life Works When 80% of Its Ocean Is Protected https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T9hjCFTwu0o
👉Living in the Maldives | How Life Works on Islands with Almost No Land  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c-8qbl4t9CI
👉Living in Tuvalu | How Life Works in a Country That Could Disappear https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XLfBG7wXwQ4 
👉Living in Orango | How Life Works Where the Family Line Follows the Mother https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HHM-JDdYQgE

What surprised you most about life in the Falkland Islands? For me, it was realizing how much distance affects everything — school, healthcare, food, transportation, even the way people work.
And here’s a tougher question: if you had to live there for a year, would you choose Stanley or a remote farm out in Camp?

I’m genuinely curious what you’d pick and why. 👇

comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: People often see isolation as a disadvantage, but this video makes it look more complicated than that.

replies.author: @RemoteEarthJourneys
replies.text: Exactly—that is the tension I wanted to preserve. Distance in the Falklands can make travel, deliveries and services harder, but it also shapes a strong sense of local self-reliance and community. Isolation is not simply good or bad; it changes what ordinary life asks of people. Which part felt most different from what you expected?
